canonical_title: Meta Q2 2026 AI spending compresses free cash flow
treatment: Repeat only for a material capex revision, new AI monetization disclosure, financing change, data-center capacity commitment, or a major cash-flow correction.
known_facts: Meta reported Q2 2026 free cash flow of $784 million, down 91% year over year, as AI infrastructure spending and other costs rose.
Meta raised the lower end of its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $130 billion while retaining a $145 billion upper bound.
Quarterly revenue rose 28% year over year to $60.8 billion, while investors focused on the cost and monetization risk of Meta's AI strategy.

FOLLOW_UP 2026-10-26: Meta announced equity fundraising plans totaling up to $95 billion for AI infrastructure, with roughly $35 billion common/preferred offerings launched and a separate up-to-$60 billion ATM program planned after Class C begins trading, expected Q1 2027.
Reuters reported Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated potential interest in purchasing up to $5 billion combined of Class A stock; this is interest, not completed investment.
Reuters reported Meta Q3 2026 free cash flow negative $2.12 billion, with 2026 capex guidance $135-$145 billion; the new financing is distinct from previously covered Q2 capex compression.

FOLLOW_UP 2026-10-27: Meta raised the total announced maximum equity fundraising from $95B to $97.5B, increasing the common-stock offering from $22.5B to $25B at $625 per share; $12.5B preferred depositary shares and up-to-$60B future ATM remain separate components.

FOLLOW_UP 2026-10-27: NVIDIA publicly committed to a planned $3B investment in Meta's equity offering, with expanded collaboration to optimize Muse model training/inference and consideration of NVIDIA OpenShell/Sentry; closing is not yet verified.
reinclude_only_if: Meta materially changes 2026 or 2027 AI capital expenditure guidance.
Meta discloses concrete revenue, subscription, business-agent, or compute-resale economics for its AI investments.
A major financing, data-center, chip-supply, or restructuring decision changes the practical interpretation of the buildout.
Meta prices/completes the new $35B offerings, launches the $60B ATM program, or reports material changes to financing terms and chip-vendor participation.
Meta completes pricing and closing, or NVIDIA's announced $3B investment closes and definitive allocation/conditions are disclosed.
